items.text: The agent's responses are exposed as text that the screen reader reads in full.
The code editor, chat box and preview have meaningful labels.
Any model preview or rendering has a text alternative describing what it shows.
Status and errors are not conveyed only by colour, icons or visuals.
The user is told when the agent starts, is working and has finished.
After each request, the agent states what changed in the model (which parts, which dimensions).
The user can review the sequence of edits made so far.
The agent reports when it did something different from what was asked.
Every function (prompting, editing, rendering, exporting) works by keyboard alone.
Navigation between chat, code and preview is consistent and predictable.
Focus lands somewhere sensible after each response or render.
The user can interrupt or cancel the agent mid-task.
Errors in the code or the model are announced in an accessible form.
The user can undo or revert a bad edit.
The tool gives a non-visual way to check that the model matches the request, such as dimensions, a part list or a geometric description.
Help and documentation are readable with a screen reader.
It works with the screen reader and browser the auditor uses.
The user can control how much detail the agent gives when describing the model.
Output can be inspected in more than one non-visual way (text, audio or tactile export).
Settings and preferences persist between sessions.
